place.why: Address in San Francisco, CA; mention of public hospital

summary: At Zuckerberg San Francisco General, complaints start with the hospital’s Patient Experience team, and independent facility complaints go to the California Department of Public Health through Cal Health Find. Because this is a San Francisco public hospital, a money claim for harm starts with a City claim within 6 months, then California malpractice court deadlines and notice rules apply. You can get records through SF.gov/MyChart, and the Health Consumer Alliance offers free help.

steps.body: Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center
steps.what: ZSFG is part of the SF Health Network operated by the San Francisco Department of Public Health. The hospital tells patients to contact Patient Experience Services and says they may submit a Patient Concern Statement; it will investigate and tell the patient the outcome. The provider page does not state its own filing deadline or response-time target, but the federal hospital rule requires a grievance process for prompt resolution with stated time frames.
steps.wall: No online form found; the site route only reached a downloadable Patient Concern Statement PDF.
points: ZSFG says to contact Patient Experience Services to help resolve concerns.
Patients may submit a Patient Concern Statement describing the concern and the resolution they want.
ZSFG says an investigation will be conducted and the patient will be informed of the outcome.
Federal hospital rules require a process for prompt resolution of patient grievances.
Federal hospital rules require the grievance process to specify time frames for review and response.
steps.appliesIf: Care at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center, a public hospital in the SF Health Network operated by San Francisco Department of Public Health.
alternatives: California Department of Public Health complaint through Cal Health Find
missing: The provider’s own current written deadline for filing a complaint, if any
The provider’s own stated response-time target, if any

steps.what: CDPH independently takes complaints about licensed health-care facilities, including hospitals. It says anyone can file, and the most direct route is the Cal Health Find complaint path, which starts by searching for the facility.
points: Anyone can file a complaint against a health-care facility.
CDPH says filing through Cal Health Find is the most direct way.
The Cal Health Find complaint page starts with a Facility Name search field.
For general acute care hospitals and other non-long-term-care facilities, complaints indicating an ongoing threat of imminent danger of death or serious bodily harm must be completed within 45 days.
steps.appliesIf: Complaints about a licensed California hospital, including public hospital care at ZSFG.
alternatives: Complain first or in parallel to ZSFG Patient Experience Services
missing: The exact fields that appear after selecting the facility in Cal Health Find

sources.quote: Anyone can file a complaint against a health-care facility -- a patient or facility resident, a relative or friend, even a general member of the public.
Filing a complaint through the California Health Facilities Information Database (Cal Health Find) is the most direct way.
Complaint Against a Health Care Facility/Provider
Facility Name
Enter Facility Name or City

Complaint investigations involving general acute care hospitals and other non-long-term care facilities must be completed within 45 days if the allegation indicates an ongoing threat of imminent danger of death, or serious bodily harm.

steps.body: City and County of San Francisco
steps.what: Because ZSFG is in the SF Health Network operated by the San Francisco Department of Public Health, a damages claim for harm from care there starts with the City and County of San Francisco claim route. If the matter is not resolved, California malpractice court rules then apply, including the malpractice limitation period, a 90-day notice before suit, and California’s non-economic-damages cap.
steps.deadline: "File claims for personal injury, personal property damage, death or loss, or damage to crops within 6 months of the incident."
points: "File claims for personal injury, personal property damage, death or loss, or damage to crops within 6 months of the incident."
"They must be mailed or hand- delivered."
"Allow up to 45 days for the Claims Division to process and investigate your claim."

"the time for the commencement of action shall be three years after the date of injury or one year after the plaintiff discovers, or through the use of reasonable diligence should have discovered, the injury, whichever occurs first."
"No action based upon the health care provider’s professional negligence may be commenced unless the defendant has been given at least 90 days’ prior notice of the intention to commence the action."
requires: Start with the City and County of San Francisco claim route because the hospital is operated by San Francisco Department of Public Health
Before a malpractice lawsuit, give the defendant at least 90 days’ written notice of intent to sue
steps.appliesIf: Claim for injury from care at ZSFG, a public hospital in the SF Health Network operated by San Francisco Department of Public Health.

sources.quote: File claims for personal injury, personal property damage, death or loss, or damage to crops within 6 months of the incident.
They must be mailed or hand- delivered.
Allow up to 45 days for the Claims Division to process and investigate your claim.

In an action for injury or death against a health care provider based upon such person’s alleged professional negligence, the time for the commencement of action shall be three years after the date of injury or one year after the plaintiff discovers, or through the use of reasonable diligence should have discovered, the injury, whichever occurs first.
No action based upon the health care provider’s professional negligence may be commenced unless the defendant has been given at least 90 days’ prior notice of the intention to commence the action.

steps.what: Bay Area Legal Aid offers free civil help for qualified low-income Bay Area residents, but its listed health-care work is about coverage, services, equipment, and healthcare-related debt, not malpractice damages claims. For private counsel, California allows contingency fees in malpractice cases but caps them. LawHelpCA offers a statewide legal-help finder by location and topic.
points: "Free to qualified low-income residents living in the Bay Area"
"We help low-income individuals with legal issues regarding coverage, services, equipment, and healthcare related debt."
"Search your legal issue below to find a contact."

"Twenty-five percent of the dollar amount recovered if the recovery is pursuant to settlement agreement and release of all claims executed by all parties thereto prior to a civil complaint or demand for arbitration being filed."
"Thirty-three percent of the dollar amount recovered if the recovery is pursuant to settlement, arbitration, or judgment after a civil complaint or demand for arbitration is filed."
steps.appliesIf: Adult seeking civil legal help in the Bay Area; malpractice damages cases usually need private counsel rather than BayLegal’s listed health-access work.
alternatives: State Bar certified lawyer referral service / SF-Marin LRIS
missing: Whether the patient meets Bay Area Legal Aid’s income and other eligibility rules
Whether any legal-aid program in the patient’s county will take a malpractice-damages case

steps.what: For suspected acute hand or wrist trauma when initial radiographs are negative or equivocal, the American College of Radiology publishes the Appropriateness Criteria used across U.S. practice to guide next imaging. Its acute hand and wrist trauma guidance says repeat radiographs in 10–14 days, MRI without IV contrast, and CT without IV contrast are usually appropriate.
points: The guidance specifically addresses suspected acute hand or wrist trauma with negative or equivocal initial radiographs.
Repeat radiography in 10–14 days is listed as usually appropriate.
MRI without IV contrast is listed as usually appropriate.
CT without IV contrast is listed as usually appropriate.
steps.appliesIf: Clinical imaging guidance for acute hand/wrist trauma in U.S. practice, relevant to a possible missed scaphoid fracture after an initially negative X-ray.

steps.body: San Francisco Health Network / Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital
steps.what: Patients can ask for copies of records online through MyChart, by mail, or in person through the San Francisco Health Network records process. SF.gov gives the office location at ZSFG and says the records office will get back within 7 to 10 business days.
steps.deadline: "We will get back to you within 7 to 10 business days."

The online route is MyChart.
The SF.gov page says to stop by the office and fill out the form for in-person requests.
SF.gov says the office will get back within 7 to 10 business days.
alternatives: Mail the completed authorization form with ID
Bring the completed form and valid photo ID in person

Whether they want the full chart, radiology images, or a narrower set of records
